title: Operator journey microtask mapping & error-recovery usability notes
body:
Summary:

This document captures findings from two moderated usability sessions and three asynchronous pilot runs with platform operators (internal SREs and two customer platform engineers) focused on the console flows for: model route creation, fallback policy editing, and diagnosing request-level failures. Goal was to map operator microtasks, surface friction points for rapid incident response, and propose wireframe-level fixes that reduce MTTI (mean time to investigate) for degradation events.

Participants and context:
- Sessions: 2024-11-06 (moderated, 2 SREs), 2024-11-08 (moderated, 1 customer platform eng), asynchronous pilot 2024-11-09–11 (3 engineers across Hosted and Dedicated customers).
- Personas: "On-call SRE", "Platform engineer (customer)" and "Console operator (internal runbook user)".
- Tasks tested: create new model route with canary + fallback; simulate model OOM and exercise fallback policy; investigate spike in token latency for a specific customer route and apply temporary throttling.

Methodology:
- Think-aloud moderated sessions (45–60m).
- Time-on-task measured, key taps/clicks logged.
- Post-task SUS-style quick questionnaire + freeform feedback.
- Screen recordings reviewed and annotated.

Key observations (high level):
1) Microtask fragmentation: operators treat route creation as ~6 microtasks (pick model variant, set latency SLO, attach rollout policy, configure fallback, set billing/tenant mapping, add tags). The console currently exposes these as a single long form — users wanted a stepwise microtask flow with inline validation and shortcuts.
2) Error-recovery visibility gap: when a request gets routed to a fallback model (e.g., quantized variant), the activity feed shows a single "fallback applied" line without contextual telemetry (latency delta, token count, error ratio). Operators had to jump to the observability tab and filter by route id — slow.
3) Canary rollouts are hard to snapshot: users expected a quick visual compare of baseline vs canary (per-token cost delta, 95th latency, recent quality regression flag). The console only surfaces a graph per model independently.
4) Missing suggested remediation: when an OOM occurs, the UI shows logs but does not suggest remediation steps (e.g., reduce max_tokens, switch to a smaller variant, force reroute) or allow pre-populated runbook snippets to execute.
5) Rapid throttling is obscured: throttling controls are buried under "rate limits" page; in incidents operators wanted a one-click "throttle route" in the route action menu.

Direct quotes (verbatim):
- "I don't want to fill out an entire form to test a canary. Give me a quick seed option for a smoke rollout." — SRE participant 1
- "Seeing 'fallback applied' is not enough — I need to know if my SLA will still be met." — Customer platform engineer

Severity & frequency matrix (qualitative):
- High severity, high frequency: error-recovery visibility gap, need for instant throttle (observed repeatedly across both moderated sessions).
- High severity, medium frequency: canary comparators and remediation suggestions (critical during incidents, not used daily).
- Medium severity: microtask fragmentation (annoyance, slows route creation).

Wireframe writeups / quick fixes (low-cost prototypes):
1) Microtask flow (3-step compact modal):
   - Step A: Model & variant (with quick presets: "fast-low-cost", "balanced", "high-quality").
   - Step B: SLA & rollout (percent slider + seed toggle for smoke test).
   - Step C: Fallback & runbook (select fallback variant + option to attach prewritten remediation snippet).
   Rationale: reduces cognitive load and allows keyboard shortcuts for repeat creation.

2) Incident action bar (global sticky at top of route page):
   - Buttons: "Throttle 50%", "Throttle 10%", "Switch to fallback", "Open runbook".
   - Each button opens a small confirmation modal with predicted SLO/Cost delta.
   Rationale: One-click mitigations reduce MTTI in severity incidents.

3) Fallback detail expansion:
   - Expandable inline card when fallback triggers showing: time of trigger, cause (OOM/latency/error), baseline vs fallback 95p latency, token delta, recent quality signals.
   Rationale: keeps investigation in context without tab switching.

4) Canary comparator overlay:
   - Small overlay comparing baseline and canary for the last 15m with three sparklines (latency P50/P95, error-rate, tokens-per-request) and a cost delta estimate.

Backlog grooming — prioritized tickets (initial estimates):
- P0: Add "Throttle" actions to route action menu + incident action bar. (JIRA-CORE-2143) — 3 dev days + 1 UX day.
- P0: Inline fallback detail card (server needs to surface fallback event metadata) — cross-team: serving-runtime + backend telemetry. (JIRA-OBS-2901) — 5 dev days + 2 UX days.
- P1: Microtask 3-step modal for quick route creation with presets — design + front-end only. (JIRA-UX-3412) — 8 dev days.
- P1: Canary comparator overlay (frontend visual + small telemetry endpoint) — (JIRA-UX-3419) — 6 dev days.
- P2: Runbook snippets: store, attach, and execute from console (security review for actions) — (JIRA-SEC-1186) — 10 dev days + security.

Open questions / risks:
- Telemetry availability: serving runtime must emit richer fallback metadata (cause, latency delta). Need an infra commit from observability to add these fields.
- Permissions model for "execute runbook snippets" needs review: we must avoid surfacing privileged actions to non-admins.
- Cost estimation accuracy: Providing live cost delta for rollouts requires a fast estimation API — current cost pipeline is batchy.

Next steps / recommended research: 
- Sprint 1 (2 weeks): Implement P0 items as an incident playbook — narrow rollout internal-only, collect MTTI metrics.
- Quick A/B test: swap current route form for microtask modal for 10% of internal traffic and measure time-to-create and error rates.
- Follow-up moderated sessions after P0: 2 internal SREs + 1 customer platform eng to validate changes (target date 2024-12-05).

Appendix — session notes (short):
- 2024-11-06-SRE-1: Spent 7:34 on canary creation; confusion around "fallback priority" ordering; used console search to find route id to correlate logs.
- 2024-11-08-CustEng: Triggered simulated OOM; expected suggested remediation; manually edited route to fallback variant (4 clicks) but could not see immediate cost impact.
- 2024-11-11-Async-Pilot-2: Reported that throttling buried in rate-limits added ~8 minutes to their incident response time.

Note: prototypes attached in Figma link (linked_artifacts). Full recordings stored in internal drive under /recordings/console-operator-nov2024 (request access if needed).

Prepared by: Sophie Chen (UX Researcher)
Reviewers: Dylan Park (Product), Miguel Ortega (Observability)

Status: In review — please add comments inline in Confluence page reference (linked_artifacts) or raise JIRA tickets for new issues.
